loop: gauntlet: a builder and a separate critic with fresh context per piece. The critic runs ours next to native, names the biggest gap, and the piece loops until the critic picks ours.

items.title: #7 chunking, hashing and block store
items.detail: Round 1 F1-F10 fixed and held (1800 simulated power-loss cases: 0 acked blocks lost, 0 wrong bytes; 3 min 8-thread stress 27.7M ops, 0 errors; builds on Rust 1.89). Round 2 verdict: NOT mergeable. N1: a benign torn write becomes permanent 'corruption' after the next sync moves the watermark over the gap (about 7% of simulated crashes), and cowfs-core refuses to mount on it. N2: watermark ahead of the packs makes sync() silently stop fsyncing. N3: a deleted middle pack is not reported. N4: a failed pack roll wedges puts forever (AlreadyExists). N5: the 64 MiB resync budget can drop a whole damaged pack from the index (1100 damaged records lost all 4095 blocks, ~3000 valid). Also 8 real mutant gaps. Builder fixing (header CRC format change, torn-tail sidecar, transactional roll, pack manifest, salvage API). | Update: builder pushed round-2 fixes (head 7b93448); I re-ran: 85 crate tests pass, fmt/clippy clean, scope clean. Awaiting its final report and a round-3 look at the recovery changes.

items.title: #8 Merkle tree and O(1) writable snapshots
items.detail: Critic verdict: NOT mergeable. Tree, refcounts and crash atomicity held against a harsher harness (reordering, 512 B/4 KiB tearing, every-event crash, snapshot-remove crash). Blockers: F1 before_sync hook runs BEFORE the closure so a put-then-set_content batch made durable metadata reference unsynced blocks in 10 of 30 commits; F2 clean drop makes metadata durable even when the hook fails; F3 inode numbers are reused after a crash (100 creates, crash, next ino 2), aliasing stale handles. Also: no flush timer, lost fsync makes the file unopenable (fails closed), lookup 39 us at 1M, 1.7 ms per unbatched op, remove_snapshot stalls writers 837 ms, no magic check, 4 mutants survive. Builder fixing with API changes for core listed in docs/v1-meta.md. | Update: builder pushed fixes (head 67496d2, CI now green); I re-ran: 70 crate tests pass, fmt/clippy clean, scope clean. Awaiting its final report. Core must re-merge this branch and the store branch (its macOS CI failure is a meta test fixed here).

items.title: #10 garbage collection
#11 Linux FUSE mount
items.detail: Critic findings fixed, re-verified by me at 98c0f24: 43 unit tests on Mac, and in the Linux VM 46 unit + 39 mount + 5 regress tests pass, no mounts left. Defaults now safe: ttl 1 s, keep_cache off, opt-in SoleWriter with an Invalidator; Vfs panics become EIO then a clean unmount; keyed-lane worker pool (slow read no longer delays stat: 856 ms to 0.2 ms, builder's n=1); signal cleanup and stale-mount sweep; inode-reuse paranoid mode. Decisions for lead: cross-adapter permission policy (FUSE denies later O_WRONLY on a 0444 file, NFS allows), SoleWriter wiring by core/control plane (invalidate from outside Vfs calls), add 'Ino never reused' text to architecture doc (done on v1/vfs-trait), add a Linux mount CI job (command in report). 2 survivors: one equivalent, one control.

items.title: #12 macOS NFS loopback mount
items.detail: Round-1 findings fixed with regression tests (I re-ran: 38 nfsserve/adapter + protocol tests pass, fmt/clippy clean, CI green): reference-balance leak, AppleDouble Translate (sidecar to xattrs, no sidecar inodes; 200 files = 200 inodes vs 400), one-shot MNT + keyed MAC handles + generations, DoS bounds, retransmission reply cache, inode-reuse STALE, signal cleanup + stale-mount sweep. Mutants 21/22 killed. Caveats: latency at load 42-65 (inline_metadata helps writes and reads, noisy), no before/after RPC baseline, lsof peer-uid check adds almost nothing, RSS soak 3 to 40 MiB unexplained, real files named ._x invisible under Translate. Translate is new stateful code, so a round-2 critic is attacking it. | Update: #34 found a real bug: reply cache ignores the connection (cross-connection xid collision replays the wrong reply). Builder fixing while the round-2 critic reviews.

items.title: #26 cowfs-core: Vfs over store and meta
items.detail: Critic verdict: NOT mergeable. F1 deadlock: ensure_file holds the node write lock then takes the meta read lock while commit holds meta write then node read (repro hangs; builder's stress/kill9 never hit it). F2 promote_base removes base then forks: a failed fork loses base. F3 one corrupt block wedges the whole snapshot (fsync, readdir, fork, merkle_root all return Corrupt; other files' acked data lost at reopen) and a partial overwrite inside a corrupt chunk succeeds. Also: virtual inos reused across restart (wrong bytes), snapshot names accept .git/newline/ESC and case/NFC duplicates unlike the CLI, readdir flushes unrelated dirty data (48 MiB, 179 ms), alias table unbounded (469 MB after 500k creates), zero-id hole refs look dangling to GC. Held up: durability ordering, fsx 20k ops vs model, 60 s of overlapping writers (0 torn), hook failure recovery, EIO on corrupt reads. Bench (load 11-15): seq read 1351 MiB/s (13.6x slower than APFS page cache), 4K read 21.6k/s, seq write+fsync 390 MiB/s, lookups faster than std::fs. Builder fixing and re-merging fixed store and meta.

items.title: #34 cowfs-vfs-path: run the suite on native filesystems and through mounts
items.detail: Suite run on APFS, btrfs, ext4, FUSE and NFS. Posix level (56 checks): 0 failures natively and through FUSE; NFS mount 10 (9 silly rename, 1 AppleDouble Translate hides ._ names). FUSE adapter: no bug. NFS adapter bug found: the reply cache ignores the connection, so a second connection's identical xid replays the first connection's reply and the call never runs (sent to the #12 builder). Suite level corrections sent to the #29 builder (torn reads on ext4/btrfs/tmpfs at 512/4096 B, statfs files=0 on btrfs, com.apple.* xattrs, atime-only ctime, xattr name prefix, LINK_MAX hang). Client-side, not adapter: sparse blocks, statfs caching, silly rename. 2 unexplained flakes.
